rv.q: In texture, the piece (translated by William Gregory) feels akin to a Caryl Churchill play, with its teasing obliqueness and surprising, dark shafts of humour.
It might, though, leave several audience members scratching their heads.
Every element of this performance works together beautifully.

cn.t: Pablo Manzi's sharp, fragmentary debut explores violence and loneliness across Latin America through five brief, unrelated scenes. Critics find the Chilean play compelling if uneven, with praise for its ambitious scope and timely themes.
